# Home advantage  

In order to investigate the home advantage in nba, let's calculate

* Number of games the teams won and lost in home and away games separately.
* Average number of points scored by the teams in home and away games.
* Total number of points scored by the teams in home and away games.

```{r}
nba_standings <- nba_east 
data("nba2009_2021")

nba_won_count_h_t <- nba2009_2021 %>%
  group_by(home.TEAM_NAME, SEASON_ID) %>%
  summarize(H_L = sum(home.PTS < away.PTS),H_W = sum(home.PTS > away.PTS), 
            MEAN_HP = mean(home.PTS), TOTAL_HP = sum(home.PTS)) %>%
  rename(TEAM_NAME = home.TEAM_NAME)

nba_won_count_a_t <- nba2009_2021 %>%
  group_by(away.TEAM_NAME, SEASON_ID) %>%
  summarize(A_L = sum(home.PTS > away.PTS),A_W = sum(home.PTS < away.PTS), 
            MEAN_AP = mean(away.PTS), TOTAL_AP = sum(away.PTS)) %>%
  rename(TEAM_NAME = away.TEAM_NAME)



```

## Home advantage

* Joining the two dataframes together to get the teams' statistics seperated in home and away games
* Joining the resulted dataframe with standings to get the teams rank that year.

```{r}
nba_teams_stats <- inner_join(nba_won_count_h_t, nba_won_count_a_t, 
                              by = c("TEAM_NAME", "SEASON_ID")) %>%
                              distinct()
nba_standings$Season <- as.character(nba_standings$Season)

nba_teams_stats <- inner_join(nba_teams_stats, nba_standings,
  by = c("TEAM_NAME" = "Team", "SEASON_ID" = "Season")) %>%
  arrange(SEASON_ID, Rank)

head(nba_teams_stats, 3)
```

## Home advantage
Let's define a few metrics for analysing the home advantage. 

* On average home many more points are scored by the home teams  
**(MEAN_HP - MEAN_AP)**
* How many more games do the teams win in the games where they are the home team  
**(HW - A_W)**
* Percentage of games won in home games **(H_W / (H_W + A_W))**
* Percentage of points scored in home games **(TOTAL_HP / (TOTAL_HP + TOTAL_AP))**

After calculating the metrics will count the averages and visualize over time.
```{r}
nba_teams_stats_ha <- nba_teams_stats %>%
  mutate(
    HA1 = MEAN_HP - MEAN_AP, 
    HA2 = H_W - A_W, 
    HA3 = H_W /  (H_W + A_W) , 
    HA4 = TOTAL_HP / (TOTAL_HP + TOTAL_AP)) %>%
  rename_with(toupper)

ha_stats_by_season <- nba_teams_stats_ha %>%
  group_by(SEASON_ID) %>%
  summarise(mean_HA1 = mean(HA1), mean_HA2 = mean (HA2),
  mean_HA3 = mean(HA3), mean_HA4 = mean(HA4))
```

## Home advantage
\tiny
```{r, out.height="65%", fig.align='center'}
ggplot(ha_stats_by_season,aes(x = SEASON_ID, group = 1)) + 
  geom_line(aes(y = mean_HA1)) + geom_line(aes(y = mean_HA2), color = "red") + 
  geom_line(aes(y = mean_HA3), color = "blue") + geom_line(aes(y = mean_HA4), color = "green") +
  ggtitle("Home Advantage in NBA over years") + xlab('Season') + ylab('Home Advantage')
```

## Home advantage

Interpretations from the previous plot.  

* The ratios show almost the same result.
* The differences in between the number of points and number of games won  
varies over time and are independent of each other.

Scoring more points in home games does not guarantee to win more games at home.
We can see multiple cases of decrease in the difference of the points that 
results to an increas in the difference of number of games won at home.  

Let's try to pick the best metric for the home advantage by calculating the metric's  
correlation to the number of games won at home. 

\tiny
```{r}
(cor(nba_teams_stats_ha$HA1, nba_teams_stats_ha$H_W))
(cor(nba_teams_stats_ha$HA2, nba_teams_stats_ha$H_W))
(cor(nba_teams_stats_ha$HA3, nba_teams_stats_ha$H_W))
(cor(nba_teams_stats_ha$HA4, nba_teams_stats_ha$H_W))
```
## Home advantage

```{r, out.height="65%", fig.align='center'}
ggplot(nba_teams_stats_ha, aes(x = as.factor(RANK), y = HA3)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  ggtitle("Home advantage by Rank") +
  xlab("Rank") +
  ylab("Home advantage")
```

## Home advantage

Interpretations from the previous plot.  

* The home advantage gets balanced for the teams in the middle.
* The home advantage is not a key factor for teams in the top of the table.
* The teams in the bottom of the table less outliers,

Let's build a model to identify the significance of the rank for home advantage.

## Home advantage

Home advantage is not a significant factor for the teams in the top of the table,
but is a very important factor for the teams in the bottom.

\tiny
```{r}
nba_teams_stats_ha$RANK <- as.factor(nba_teams_stats_ha$RANK)

model <- lm(HA3 ~ RANK, data = nba_teams_stats_ha)

summary(model)
```
# Power Ratings

Let's try to identify the relationship betwen power rating of the team 
and its chances of winning the game in National Hockey League.
```{r}
nhl_games <- read.csv('../data/game.csv')

nhl_games <- nhl_games %>%
  mutate(outcome = ifelse(grepl("home win", outcome), "HW", "AW")) %>%
  select(game_id,season,date_time_GMT,home_team_id,away_team_id, 
         home_goals, away_goals, outcome)

head(nhl_games,3)
```

## Power Ratings

Data preperation. Converging the dataset to long format to calculate cumulative 
goals scored and conceded.

```{r}
nhl_games_long <- nhl_games %>%
  reshape2::melt(id.vars = c("game_id","season","date_time_GMT",
                             "home_team_id","away_team_id", "outcome"),
                 measure.vars = c("home_goals", "away_goals"),
                 variable.name = "h_a") %>%
  arrange(game_id)

nhl_games_long <- nhl_games_long %>% 
  mutate(team1_id = ifelse(h_a == 'home_goals', home_team_id, away_team_id),
         team2_id = ifelse(h_a == 'home_goals', away_team_id, home_team_id)) %>%
  select(game_id,season,date_time_GMT,team1_id,team2_id,h_a, value,outcome)

head(nhl_games_long)
```

## Power Ratings

Calculating the sum of the goals scored and conceded by each team in the last 5 games before each game.

```{r}
nhl_games_long <- nhl_games_long %>%
  group_by(season, team1_id) %>%
  mutate(cum_sc = rollsum(value, k = 5, fill = NA, align="right")) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(season, team2_id) %>%
  mutate(cum_c = rollsum(value, k = 5, fill = NA, align="right")) %>% 
  tidyr::drop_na() %>%
  as.data.frame()

head(nhl_games_long,3)
```


## Power Ratings

Converting back to wide format and calculating the power ratings.  

* Home team's power rating = Number of goals scored in the last 5 games - Number of goals conceded in the last 5 games.
* The same calculation is done for away team.
* Calculating the power difference of the game.

\tiny
```{r}
nhl_games_wide = reshape(nhl_games_long, direction = "wide", timevar = "h_a", 
  idvar = "game_id", v.names = c("value","cum_sc", "cum_c")) %>%
  mutate(powerhome = cum_sc.home_goals - cum_c.home_goals,
         poweraway = cum_sc.away_goals - cum_c.away_goals,
         powerdiff = powerhome - poweraway) %>%
  select(game_id,season,date_time_GMT,team1_id,team2_id, value.home_goals,
       value.away_goals,cum_sc.home_goals, cum_c.home_goals, 
       cum_sc.away_goals,cum_c.away_goals, powerhome, poweraway, powerdiff, outcome) %>% 
  tidyr::drop_na()

head(nhl_games_wide, 3)
```

## Power Ratings

Calculating the frequencies

```{r}
freqs = dcast(nhl_games_wide, powerdiff ~ outcome)
head(freqs, 3)
```


## Power Ratings

Calculating the relative frequencies

```{r}
freqs_rel = data.frame(freqs, freqs[,2:3]/rowSums(freqs[,2:3]))
head(freqs_rel)

freqs_rel[freqs_rel$powerdiff == 0,]
```

## Power Ratings
\tiny
```{r, out.height="65%", fig.align='center'}
ggplot(freqs_rel, aes(x = powerdiff, y = HW)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  ggtitle("Number of games won by home teams vs Powerdiff") +
  xlab("Powerdiff") +
  ylab("Number of games won")
```

## Power Ratings
Interpretations from the previous plot.  

* With the increase of power rating the percentage of the games won by the home team increases.
* Very few games when the powerdiff was a high number in favor of the home or away team.

## Power Ratings
\tiny
```{r, out.height="65%", fig.align='center'}
ggplot(freqs_rel, aes(x = powerdiff, y = HW.1)) + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = F) +
  geom_point() +
  ggtitle("Home teams' game winning percentage vs Powerdiff") +
  xlab("Home games winning percentage") +
  ylab("Powerdiff")
```

## Power Ratings
Interpretations from the previous plot.  

* The variables do not seem to have a relationship.

## Power Ratings
* Small correlation coefficient.
* Almost no significance for the powerdiff and weak predictive power.

\tiny
```{r}
(cor(freqs_rel$powerdiff, freqs_rel$HW.1))
summary(lm(HW.1 ~ powerdiff, data = freqs_rel))
```

## Power Ratings

Adjusting the calculation strategy to have a power rating relative to the opponent.

* Home team's power rating = Number of goals scored in the last 5 games - Number of goals conceded in the last 5 games by the opponent.
* The same calculation is done for away team.
* Calculating the power difference of the game.

\tiny
```{r}
nhl_games_wide = reshape(nhl_games_long, direction = "wide", timevar = "h_a", 
  idvar = "game_id", v.names = c("value","cum_sc", "cum_c")) %>%
  mutate(powerhome = cum_sc.home_goals - cum_c.away_goals,
         poweraway = cum_sc.away_goals - cum_c.home_goals,
         powerdiff = powerhome - poweraway) %>%
  select(game_id,season,date_time_GMT,team1_id,team2_id, value.home_goals,
       value.away_goals,cum_sc.home_goals, cum_c.home_goals, 
       cum_sc.away_goals,cum_c.away_goals, powerhome, poweraway, powerdiff, outcome) %>% 
  tidyr::drop_na()

head(nhl_games_wide, 3)
```

## Power Ratings

Calculating the relative frequencies

```{r}
freqs = dcast(nhl_games_wide, powerdiff ~ outcome)
freqs_rel = data.frame(freqs, freqs[,2:3]/rowSums(freqs[,2:3]))
head(freqs_rel)

freqs_rel[freqs_rel$powerdiff == 0,]
```

## Power Ratings

\tiny
```{r, out.height="65%", fig.align='center'}
ggplot(freqs_rel, aes(x = powerdiff, y = HW.1)) + 
  geom_smooth(method = "glm", 
    method.args = list(family = "binomial"), 
    se = TRUE) +
  geom_point() +
  ggtitle("Home teams' game winning percentage vs Powerdiff") +
  xlab("Home games winning percentage") +
  ylab("Powerdiff")
```

## Power Ratings

Interpretations from the previous plot.  

* The variables are now strongly related.
* The relationship is not linear.
* Logistic regression model fits the data very well.

Let's try fitting a linear model.

\tiny
```{r}
(cor(freqs_rel$powerdiff, freqs_rel$HW.1))
summary(lm(HW.1 ~ powerdiff, data = freqs_rel))

```

## Power Ratings

Fitting a logarithmic regession (logit) model.

* Strong predictive power.
* High significance for powerdiff.

Better to take the linear model, as the difference is not huge and linear also performs pretty good and in addition it is easier to interpret.

\tiny
```{r}
model <- glm(HW.1 ~ powerdiff, data = freqs_rel, family = binomial(link = "logit"))
(r_squared <- with(summary(model), 1 - deviance/null.deviance))
(summary(model))
```
